**Finding submitted — AUDIT: deviation (fallback redline).**

- **Investigation:** No clause uses "audit"/"inspect"/"verify" anywhere in the document. I checked all planner candidates (11.3 Suspected Violations, 11.5 Capacity Planning, 13.2 AUP) plus 5.3 Security, 11.2, 11.6, 12.1 License and 14.17 Limitation of Licenses. Neither 11.5 nor 13.2 contains any monitoring or usage-verification right.
- **Responsive clause:** § 11.3 — IBM "reserves the right to investigate potential violations" of Customer's AUP warranty, with no frequency cap, no prior notice for the investigation itself (the notice in p0137 is only an "attempt" before access restriction or Content removal), and no cost allocation; p0138 adds an open-ended duty to give IBM "all relevant information ... at IBM's request."
- **Classification:** Unlimited/unannounced verification sits in walk-away territory, so the fallback is failed on material terms.
- **Redline:** One insert after p0138 carrying exactly the three fallback elements — once per year, 15 days' prior notice, IBM bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%. No preferred-only terms (independent auditor, off-site, no system access) were volunteered; they remain the escalation position.
